corrected_summary: Parakeet v3 advertises English and Dutch; the int8 Windows conversion still needs personal-voice and mixed-speech evaluation.
Parakeet v2 is an English-only candidate and cannot establish Dutch support.
The inspected Parakeet v3 int8 payload has encoder, decoder, joiner and tokens totaling 670,478,772 bytes; configuration and derivative notices remain separate gates.
Managed sherpa C# bindings and Windows native packages exist; ABI/RID/provider packaging must be tested in Far Flow.
Provider requests may fall back or partition onto CPU; validate actual initialization, node placement, dtype correctness and speed, rather than a provider string.
Multilingual Whisper small/turbo and quantized artifacts exist; .en variants are a different language scope.
whisper.cpp supports Windows CPU/CUDA/Vulkan build paths; tagged source and binary/nightly distribution are distinct evidence.
Compiled Core ML artifacts are platform backend outputs, not Windows runtime inputs; source models can be evaluated in different conversions.
Generic Qwen3-4B is not the Mac Instruct-2507 checkpoint. Vetted community GGUFs of the exact non-thinking checkpoint are separate candidates.
Runtime memory includes weights, KV/context and compute buffers; disk bytes alone cannot prove RTX 3070 fit.
Qwen3-ASR has documented Dutch coverage as an additional candidate, without a Windows export/provider/performance result here.
Model files exercise native parsers. Hash identity and helper processes do not establish a malicious-model sandbox.
Fn is not a universal standalone Windows trigger; an ordinary detected/rebindable key is required for a broad PC product.
RegisterHotKey provides press notification, not a global key-up contract for hold-to-talk.
Slow low-level hooks can cease receiving events; return immediately and use timestamped edge events. Exact timeout details have narrower independent corroboration.
WASAPI shared capture can use the endpoint mix format; ASR normalization remains an explicit contract, with application or engine conversion choices.
Direct capture clients own endpoint/format-change handling; Bluetooth communications modes expand the rate/channel test matrix.
ValuePattern sets a value, not an arbitrary caret insertion; TextPattern itself is read-only. Pattern coexistence is possible.
Ordinary SendInput is constrained by integrity levels; secure/password detection and safe copy recovery are product responsibilities.
Unicode input routes to the foreground thread, so target validation is not an atomic delivery transaction; clipboard/terminal recovery needs explicit policy.
Nonactivating HWND styles need nonactivating API use, DPI/monitor handling and a WM_MOUSEACTIVATE hover guard.
GSMTC exposes cooperating media sessions, not every audio producer; exact package/capability behavior remains a Windows spike.
Media pause success is not a causal ownership token. Retain the exact session and abandon ambiguous resume ownership.
Kill-on-last-job-handle-close supports owned lifetime; use creation-time job assignment and noninherited sole ownership to avoid the late-assignment orphan window.
As of the research date, .NET 10 is LTS; catalog metadata shows SDK 10.0.403 / runtime 10.0.14.
As of the research date, the highest stable Windows App SDK package is 2.5.1, not a newer-dated servicing patch from an older major line.
Microsoft recommends WinUI for new native Windows UI; task-specific framework tradeoffs still require a feasibility gate.
Framework runtime floors and edition-specific Windows servicing are different from the product support/test policy.
A normal full-trust WinUI MSIX is not the UWP AppContainer model; activation/manifest attributes matter.
Both .NET and Windows App SDK runtime closure matter. Single-file guidance conflicts and self-extraction is not the baseline delivery promise.
Microphone/media declarations and access depend on app model; actual signed deployment must be tested.
Normal WinUI desktop backgrounding is not UWP suspension; close/minimize/worker lifetime remain app-owned behavior.
Signing does not guarantee immediate SmartScreen reputation; actual publisher eligibility and certificate trust remain provisioning gates.
App Installer supports managed updates, but prompt/block behavior varies with app model/launch source and must be tested.
A pure native ARM64 process requires matching native binaries; emulation/ARM64EC and separate-worker architectures are distinct lanes.
This macOS planning session has no Windows execution evidence. Actual runner images differ; select an explicit VS2026 image/toolchain instead of assuming windows-2025 contains it.
The audited public Mac tree targets macOS/arm64 and has no Windows project in that revision.
The current app/artifacts are Mac-targeted and unvalidated on Windows; do not generalize that MLX/MLX Swift is universally Mac-only.
The Mac gesture starts capture on first press; 220 ms classifies release/hold behavior and 350 ms is the configured second-tap window, not a delayed start.
Full UserData backup JSON uses an explicit ISO-8601 path; dictionary-only JSON and internal SQLite serialization are different contracts.
Portable rule concepts coexist with Apple language-ID/culture behavior; full Unicode/noncascading/mixed-language parity needs expanded fixtures.
Mac bundle identifiers, integer audio device IDs and Fn preferences require explicit Windows mapping/reset policies.
The current product intentionally quits on main-window close and distinguishes minimize; source paths are not universal forced-kill runtime proof.
The Mac record reports 50 passing tests; definitions and synthetic results were corroborated, but the validator did not rerun XCTest. None is Windows evidence.
Approved F/artwork/font sources are available with separate font terms; choose independently licensed Windows icon/sound assets.
